title: What is actually being asked for — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
What is actually being asked for — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the floor. 8 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 0 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 0 pair(s); the theorems fall into 8 strand(s), the largest of 1. 3 theorem(s) name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: families.lean, sequences.lean. Built on it: demand3.lean. Checking this cluster needs 4 file(s): src/proof/demand.lean, src/proof/families.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean, src/proof/sequences.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to 98a92a92-3e41-8fdb-9f2a-2638081e4672. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (5, 0, 5, 2, 2, 3, 7). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: light.lean (3 observed, 1.15 expected, lift 2.6), energy.lean (4 observed, 1.86 expected, lift 2.15), elementary.lean (6 observed, 2.84 expected, lift 2.11). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.96; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.64. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 83.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the named results the search data asks for — Bézout’s identity (Étienne Bézout, 1779; Bachet, 1624), the Chinese remainder theorem (Sunzi, c. 3rd–5th century), and others named in their theorems Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. fibonacci_gcd_is_the_fibonacci_of_the_gcd — (List.range' 1 14).all (fun m => (List.range' 1 14).all (fun n => Families.gcd' (Sequences.fib m) (Sequences.fib n) == Sequences.fib (Families.gcd' m n))) record
  2. the_mobius_divisor_sum_is_the_identity — (List.range' 1 30).all (fun n => ((divisors n).map mu).foldl (· + ·) 0 == (if n == 1 then (1 : Int) else 0)) record
  3. the_derangement_recurrence_holds — (List.range' 2 11).all (fun n => derange n == (n - 1) * (derange (n - 1) + derange (n - 2))) ∧ derange 4 = 9 ∧ derange 5 = 44 ∧ derange 6 = 265 record
  4. legendres_three_square_theorem — (List.range 200).all (fun n => isSumOfThreeSquares n == ¬ isExcludedForm n) record
  5. five_six_one_is_the_smallest_carmichael_number — isCarmichael 561 = true ∧ (List.range' 2 559).all (fun n => ¬ isCarmichael n) record
  6. the_parity_of_popcount_is_the_xor_of_the_bits — (List.range 128).all (fun n => bitsF 10 n % 2 == (List.range' 0 8).foldl (fun acc i => (acc + (n / (2 ^ i)) % 2) % 2) 0) record
  7. factorial_seven_is_five_thousand_and_forty — Sequences.fact 7 = 5040 ∧ Sequences.fact 6 = 720 ∧ Sequences.fact 8 = 40320 record
  8. mantels_bound_is_n_squared_over_four — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => (n / 2) * (n - n / 2) == n * n / 4) record
